claims.statement: NIS2 Article 21 requires covered entities to address supply-chain security, including security-related aspects of relationships with direct suppliers and service providers, and to consider supplier-specific vulnerabilities and cybersecurity practices.

Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690 requires the digital-sector entities within its scope to maintain a direct-supplier directory and adopt supplier selection, contracting, review, and exit requirements; it is not a universal detailed template for every NIS2 sector.

ENISA's 2022 survey found broad supply-chain policy adoption but thinner staffing and budget coverage, consistent with a labour-saving managed workflow need rather than evidence of willingness to buy this particular product.

Established products already offer reusable assessments, security-information exchanges, vendor inventories, questionnaires, monitoring, and recurring reviews, so evidence reuse alone is not differentiated.

A passport operator that processes identifiable contacts or other personal data for MSP clients needs explicit controller-processor allocation, contractual instructions, security measures, and audit support under GDPR.

Hypothesis: a constrained evidence-and-expiry layer can earn adoption if it maps official guidance into an MSP's existing process and imports or exports to incumbent GRC systems; no source establishes MSP willingness to white-label it or the proposed price.

contrary_evidence: ProcessUnity already describes a one-assessment, share-many-times exchange, which directly overlaps the reusable-passport premise.
Whistic, OneTrust, Vanta, and Drata already cover security-document exchange, vendor inventories, questionnaires, evidence collection, monitoring, and recurring assessments.

The detailed requirements in Regulation 2024/2690 apply to specified digital and ICT-service entities, while obligations and enforcement details elsewhere depend on sector and national implementation; a universal NIS2 questionnaire is not established.

None of the reviewed incumbent pages publishes a directly comparable per-supplier price, and no public evidence validates MSP revenue share, white-label appetite, supplier response rates, or customer acceptance of a third-party passport.

economics.acquisition_route: Secure one paid Polish or CEE MSP design partner, prove reuse on 100-300 supplier reviews, then sell through MSP referrals and interoperable exports rather than replacing the customer's GRC suite.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated years 7-10 scenario: 30000 active supplier records at a blended 22 PLN per month produces about 7.92 million PLN ARR. At 20% EBITDA, a 5x EBITDA value, and 70% founder ownership, founder equity is about 5.54 million PLN; this excludes retained cash to avoid double counting and requires repeatable MSP activation, controlled liability, and low integration cost.
economics.founder_time: 18-25 hours weekly through design partnership and security-hardening; reduce below 15 hours only after onboarding and evidence-review operations are partner-owned.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Target 75-85% after encrypted storage, audit logging, security monitoring, and partner support; independent security reviews, insurance, and bespoke integrations are operating expenses that can depress early margins.
economics.payback: Unknown until a partner measures hours saved and activation. A go/no-go target is that the MSP's first-year fee be recoverable from documented review labour or a separately sold managed-compliance package within 12 months.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated conservative hypothesis: 18000-45000 PLN annual MSP minimum plus 12-35 PLN per active supplier-month; reviewed incumbents use demos, contact sales, or add-ons and do not supply a clean public benchmark.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Supplier reviews recur, evidence expires, contracts change, and incidents create updates; retention still depends on remaining inside the MSP workflow and exporting data cleanly.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Verified mapping history, evidence-expiry behaviour, and customer-approved reuse patterns accumulated across MSP-managed reviews
fingerprint.customer: European MSPs serving mid-market NIS2-scope organisations and the organisations' direct ICT suppliers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Paid MSP design partners followed by integration into their managed-security or compliance packages
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Permissioned evidence provenance, expiry, questionnaire mapping, and review-ledger SaaS embedded in an MSP service
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: MSP pays an annual platform minimum plus a low fee for each active supplier record under review
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A supplier is onboarded, renewed, materially changed, or implicated in an incident and current control evidence must be reviewed

founder_fit: Strong fit with structured evidence, data modelling, automation, and low-camera B2B work.
The founder can run a bounded prototype alongside employment, but secure architecture, penetration testing, and contractual review require paid specialists.
The product should never be marketed as certification, and the founder should avoid personally making supplier-security approval decisions.
MSP-led selling reduces but does not eliminate relationship-heavy enterprise discovery; a design-partner gate is needed before a full build.
risks: A stale or over-broad assertion could be relied upon in a supplier approval and create contractual, regulatory, and reputational exposure.
Centralised security evidence and contact chains create a high-value attack target and raise the product's own NIS2 and GDPR diligence burden.
Large GRC vendors or MSP platforms can bundle the narrow workflow once demand is demonstrated.
MSP concentration can turn a nominally scalable channel into bespoke integration and support work.
Questionnaire mappings can obscure customer-specific risk unless every mapping preserves source, scope, owner, expiry, and human approval.

structure.commercial_archetype: Reusable B2B credential and evidence network
structure.control_point: The evidence provenance, expiry, and human approval record inside an MSP-managed direct-supplier review
structure.critical_dependency: MSP distribution plus customer acceptance of permissioned evidence reuse without treating the record as certification

thesis: Offer European MSPs a permissioned supplier-security evidence layer that records evidence provenance and expiry, maps the same evidence into risk-specific customer questionnaires, and leaves approval and remediation decisions with the MSP or customer. The defensible wedge is not generic questionnaire automation but a narrowly scoped, MSP-operated record that can be reused across annual direct-supplier reviews without being represented as certification.
title: Supplier Security Passport
uncertainties: Whether two or more Polish or CEE MSPs will sponsor a paid design partnership and provide anonymised questionnaire corpora.
What minimum common control set can map across customer questionnaires without creating misleading equivalence.
Whether customers will accept evidence uploaded once by a supplier or insist on their own portal, attestations, or fresh audit reports.
What security architecture, insurance, and contractual liability caps enterprise buyers will require.
Whether incumbents expose sufficient import, export, or API surfaces for an MSP-owned overlay instead of forcing replacement.
